title: Player input contract — one routing table every client's reducer must reproduce

surfaces.ten-foot: Directional input moves focus: Siri Remote (tvOS), D-pad (Android TV / Google TV), keyboard arrows on a TV browser, and keyboard arrows on the web when the timeline has focus.
surfaces.touch: Direct manipulation: iPhone/iPad and Android phones/tablets. Focus states do not apply; the pointer rows below are the whole contract.
surfaces.desktop: Pointer plus keyboard on the web. Tab moves focus; arrows are global hotkeys except while the timeline has focus, where the ten-foot timeline rows apply verbatim.

notes: hide_after_ms: chrome hides this long after the last input while playing. Never while paused, failed, scrubbing, or with a menu or the info panel open.
preview_auto_commit_ms is null: a pending preview commits only on `select` (ten-foot) or pointer release (touch); it never commits on a timer.
desktop_hotkey_coalesce_ms: arrow hotkeys on the desktop body accumulate against one frozen base and issue one seek after this much quiet — the shipped web `nudge()` behaviour, kept.
skip_seconds is the only immediate seek step: the two transport buttons and the FF/REW media keys.
preview_acceleration applies to a HELD direction while scrubbing: repeats 0–4 move 10 s, 5–9 move 30 s, 10+ move 60 s. A released key resets the ladder.
vertical_seek_seconds is null: Up/Down never seek. Vertical is navigation between rows on every surface.

conditional.close: touch and desktop only — a ten-foot player exits with `back`
conditional.airplay: web, and only while the browser reports an AirPlay target

rows.notes: A corner strip over the picture, not a row in the chrome: every client that has a Close puts it there — top-trailing on the web, top-leading on iOS and on Android, where a television cannot focus it at all. `close` is last here for the same reason it was last in the transport row: the control that ends the session is the one you should not land on by accident. Nothing here is a horizontal neighbour of a transport button.
Present only while a skip-intro/credits marker is active. Sits above the timeline row, right-aligned. Reachable by `up` from the timeline; never a horizontal neighbour of anything.
Its own full-width row. The timeline is never a horizontal neighbour of a button — Left/Right on it belong to scrubbing, so a button beside it would be unreachable without a seek.

conditional.title_info: web only — the native clients put title and synopsis on the detail screen
conditional.fullscreen: web only — a native player is already full screen

rows.notes: One row on ten-foot and on wide touch/desktop. Narrow touch splits it after `spacer` into a transport line and an options line; order within each line is unchanged. `surface_placement` names the one control a surface renders somewhere else: the web puts `info` in the `bar` row, where its ✕ already lives, and the native clients keep it here.

states.hidden: Chrome hidden; the bare video surface holds focus.
states.transport: Chrome visible; focus on a transport-row or marker button.
states.timeline: Chrome visible; focus on the timeline; no preview pending.
states.scrub: Chrome visible; focus on the timeline; a preview position is pending and shown in `time_elapsed` and on the bar.
states.menu: An audio/subtitles/quality/settings menu or panel is open; focus is inside it.
states.info: The playback-info (stats) panel is open in Standard or Debug mode; focus is inside it. Mini mode does not enter this state — it is a strip and the transport stays live.

outcomes.reveal: Show chrome; focus the last focused control (initially `play_pause`). No seek.
outcomes.focus_row: Move focus within the current row or to the adjacent row per `controls.rows` order; the platform focus engine does this, the reducer only names the target row.
outcomes.focus_transport: Move focus to the transport row, restoring the last transport control (initially `play_pause`).
outcomes.toggle_play: Play/pause. Chrome reveals if hidden and the hide timer restarts.
outcomes.skip: Immediate relative seek of ±`steps.skip_seconds`. Chrome reveals if hidden.
outcomes.preview: Enter or continue `scrub`: move the pending position by the acceleration ladder; no seek, no network.
outcomes.commit: Seek to the pending position; return to `timeline` with chrome visible.
outcomes.cancel: Discard the pending position; return to `timeline`.
outcomes.close_menu: Close the open menu; focus returns to the control that opened it.
outcomes.close_info: Close the info panel; focus returns to `info`.
outcomes.menu_focus: Focus stays inside the menu (trapped) — the platform moves it among the menu's own items.
outcomes.hide: Hide chrome; remember the focused control; focus the surface.
outcomes.toggle_chrome: Touch: hide chrome if visible, else reveal.
outcomes.ignore: Nothing happens; focus does not move.

close_control.notes: The `close` control (the iOS ✕, the Android phone's back arrow, the web's ✕ Close) is not `back`. `back` is a key — Menu, BACK, Escape — and with chrome visible on ten-foot and touch it hides the chrome, which is the right answer for a key and the wrong one for a button whose only purpose is to leave: routed through `back`, the iOS ✕ hid the chrome in `transport`, closed the panel in `info`, cancelled in `scrub`, and exited in no state a viewer could tap it from, so the only way out of a film was to force-quit the app (Paul, 2026-09-03). `close` runs these outcomes in order — close whatever is open, then leave — and every row ends in `exit`. The `menu` and `info` rows say what `close` does when it is reached; a client's own modal may take the tap first — on iOS the panel's backdrop lies over the ✕, so that tap is `info × tap_surface` (`close_info`) and the ✕ exits on the next one, and Android composes no arrow while a panel is open.

desktop: `left`/`right` outside the timeline are the coalesced ±10 s hotkeys (`timings.desktop_hotkey_coalesce_ms`); `up`/`down` are no longer seeks.

`back` is Escape. With chrome visible it exits rather than hides: a pointer user has no Menu-hide idiom and the chrome hides itself. Precedence is scrub → menu → info → exit, so Escape with a menu open closes the menu, not the player.
`select` on the timeline is Enter or Space with the timeline focused. `tap_surface` is a pointer click on the video.
Tab leaves the timeline; leaving while a preview is pending is a `cancel`.
Touch on the desktop page (a tablet browser) follows the `touch` table for `tap_surface` and pointer scrubbing.
touch: Scrubbing is a drag on the timeline: pointer down = `preview` at the touch position (continuous while dragging), pointer up = `commit`. A plain tap on the bar is a `preview` + `commit` at the tap position.

`back` is the system back gesture or button (Android). iOS has no back key, and the ✕ is not `back` on either phone: it is the `close` control, which exits regardless of state after closing whatever is open — see `close_control`.
`play_pause`, `skip_back`, `skip_forward` are the headset/lock-screen/notification media commands, which work in every state.
ten-foot: `select` on the timeline (no preview pending) is play/pause, the same as clicking the bar in the Apple TV system player. It does not "engage" anything — there is no engaged state any more; a preview exists only while a pending position exists.
`play_pause` is the hardware Play/Pause button and must work in every state that lists `toggle_play`, including `transport` (today tvOS drops it while chrome is visible).
`skip_back`/`skip_forward` are MEDIA_REWIND / MEDIA_FAST_FORWARD (Android TV) — the Siri Remote has none, so tvOS has no producer for them.
`idle` fires only while playing (`timings.hidden_only_while_playing`) and only in the states that list `hide`. A paused film keeps its chrome.
